requirement: Agents SHOULD NOT anchor a file under {cite}`requirements.references.anchors` when a more precise reference is available, such as a reference attached to the Rust item that implements or tests the definition. Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST give this direction.
rationale:
structural: The text of `requirements.references.anchors.guidance` has two clauses. The first is "Agents SHOULD NOT anchor a file ... when a more precise reference is available". It governs agent behavior, not how Habeas is built. The second is "Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST give this direction". It requires the skills to contain certain content, which is an observable property of the shipped text. No clause prescribes a library, algorithm, signature, type, field, or delegation through a named interface. The skill text is itself the artifact that gives the direction. I found no alternative implementation that would keep the behavior and violate a structural clause, so no structural obligation needs implementation evidence.

The supplied roots are `assets/skills/habeas/SKILL.md` and `assets/skills/habeas/references/syntax-details.md`. Both are skill documents, and the second carries the direction in its Anchors section, `section[Syntax%20details]/section[Anchors]`. That section says to anchor a file only "when a file that implements or tests a requirement cannot carry a reference", such as a shipped skill or a copied stylesheet. It also says "Don't anchor a file whose items can carry a reference themselves", and it points to `path#selector` for one outline node. This matches the requirement's content. Whether the guidance is adequate belongs to the behavioral criterion, not to this structural check.

behavioral: The only observable obligation is that Habeas's bundled agent skills give the direction. That direction is: don't anchor a file when a more precise reference, such as one on an item, is available. The first sentence of the requirement is guidance for agents, not behavior the harness performs.

`tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[bundled_skills_limit_anchors_to_files_whose_items_cannot_carry_references]` is marked `{test}` for the requirement. It reads the `## Anchors` section of the bundled `habeas` skill's `references/syntax-details.md` through the `skill_file` and `section` helpers. It then uses `assert_text` to require two phrases:
- "When a file that implements or tests a requirement cannot carry a reference", which limits anchoring to files that cannot carry a reference.
- "Don't anchor a file whose items can carry a reference themselves", which is the prohibition.

The second phrase covers the requirement's "more precise reference" case, where an item can carry a reference. I read the actual skill text in `assets/skills/habeas/references/syntax-details.md#section[Syntax details]/section[Anchors]`. It contains both phrases, and `assert_text` fails if either is missing.

The other bundled skills, `habeas-refactor`, `habeas-requirements` and `habeas-evidence`, mention anchors only in other contexts. I read "the skills MUST give this direction" as satisfied by the skill that documents anchor syntax, so the other skills need no test.

I found no untested obligation or ambiguity.

text: :::{req} anchors.guidance

Agents SHOULD NOT anchor a file under {cite}`requirements.references.anchors` when a more precise reference is available, such as a reference attached to the Rust item that implements or tests the definition. Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST give this direction.
:::{req} anchors
A `{req}` declaration MAY list `:impl:` and `:test:` options, and an `{example}`
declaration MAY list `:test:` options, immediately after its opening fence and
before its body, one per option line, naming a project file path or
`path#selector` for one outline node under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Each anchor MUST be an `{impl}` or `{test}` edge, under
{cite}`requirements.references.roles`, from the definition to the anchored file or
node, for files that cannot or should not carry a reference themselves.
Paths MUST follow the path rules in {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`. Option lines
MUST NOT form part of the definition's text for evidence comparison or for
requirements inputs, and MUST NOT render as body text.
For each `:test:` anchor, the harness MUST include the selected file or node's
source text in the initial model request under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs` and MUST record that selection
as an evidence input under {cite}`requirements.references.evidence_coverage`,
so changing that source makes the evidence stale.
A `:impl:` anchor alone MUST NOT require an input selecting its source. A path or selector that
does not resolve to a readable, permitted file or node MUST be a validation error naming the
definition and the path; authoring MUST report it before inference. Any other option line in a `{req}` or
`{example}` declaration MUST be a validation error.
